source.title: How many samples are needed to train a deep neural network?
source.authors: Pegah Golestaneh; Mahsa Taheri; Johannes Lederer

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; it contains a few apparent typesetting/OCR artifacts, but the empirical sections and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test prediction error as sample size changes, but does not test the catalog versions: it reports no random-label fitting, interpolation-threshold width sweep, training-test gap, optimizer/batch/regularization comparison, sharpness measure, or example-removal result.
record.gate_note: The empirical tables compare how well two curves fit test-error trends. Those results bear on sample-size scaling, but not on any listed version. The paper does not report training error, so a training-test gap cannot be calculated.
record.test_reason: The study investigates prediction-loss scaling with training sample size, which none of V1–V8 names. It compares fits of two scaling curves, without testing random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architectural classification-error advantages, optimizer or batch effects, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Using Adam and including both CNNs and fully connected networks does not itself test those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their minimax lower bound and empirical fits favor 1/√n scaling over 1/n and argue that this rate cannot generally be improved. The theoretical result concerns worst-case squared prediction risk under specified distributional and weight constraints; the empirical result compares two candidate curves fitted to held-out losses.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines test-error scaling with sample size, rather than the claim versions' memorization, intervention, or gap-tracking methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture vary across the reported test-error curve fits.

fits_no_version.finding: In all eight dataset–architecture settings, c1 + α/√n fits test loss better than c2 + β/n by both MSE and R-squared.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested ReLU networks and sample-size ranges, held-out cross-entropy or regression MSE is better fit by an offset inverse-square-root curve than an offset inverse-sample-size curve.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.2 states a minimax squared prediction-risk lower bound proportional to VF√(log(d)/n) for an ℓ1-constrained ReLU network class with Gaussian inputs and independent Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the theorem's assumptions, worst-case prediction risk over the specified network class has an inverse-square-root sample-size lower bound.

record.problems: The paper reports no training error, so the training-test gap is not measured. Curve-fit comparisons do not establish a training-error-to-test-error relationship. No uncertainty estimates for the reported fit metrics are stated.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels; chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond that needed for zero training error.
CNN versus fully connected classification error and the contributions of locality, sparsity, and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD performance under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes from adapting the training recipe.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and its interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of training-test gaps and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses generalization error to mean prediction risk or test loss, rather than the training-test gap. Classification experiments measure cross-entropy, not misclassification error. Curve-fit MSE must also be distinguished from the housing model's prediction MSE. No omitted result bearing on V1–V8 was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy for random and natural labels.
Widening beyond the width needed for zero training error and the resulting test error.
A direct convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison and the effects of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large- versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses neural-network generalization and related bounds, without testing or operationally using any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The minimax lower bound and sample-size scaling experiments address a different question from V1–V8; they neither test nor use those findings.

source_check.notes: All rows report curve-fit goodness of fit, not classification error or training-test gaps. The authors-conclusion paraphrase appropriately distinguishes the constrained worst-case risk bound from empirical comparisons of two fitted curves.
